historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly separates physical inspection from software evidence, but a BMC-side RTC-bus response does not by itself demonstrate that the Strata CPU/OS RTC interface can read time.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Requires exact SMM/RTC bus, CPU/OS interface, expected address/register/time map, repeated read-only time evidence, photos and bus/clock recovery controls.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The explicit CPU/OS wording is an ownership exception to the default Wistron platform-management I2C rule; ED-01/03 require command-to-purpose fit, ED-07/08 bind target evidence, ED-11/12 prohibit unsafe retry, and ED-36/38 reserve verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: Prove that the Strata CPU/OS reaches the RTC located on the SMM through the intended physical and logical interface and reads a valid, progressing time value, rather than merely discovering an RTC-like address from the BMC.
original_method: Identify the CPU/OS-to-SMM RTC ownership and transport; bind the exact RTC device/driver, SMM connector, bus/address or other interface and read semantics; have an operator inspect and photograph the physical path; collect read-only OS RTC inventory, driver binding, status and repeated timestamped time samples; compare them with an approved trusted reference and tolerance; preserve kernel/platform-management errors and stop without setting time, writing registers, resetting a bus or retrying automatically.
manual_activity: An operator identifies and photographs the Strata CPU-to-RTC-on-SMM connection and confirms the populated SMM/RTC hardware; the owner supplies the authoritative CPU/OS interface map and time oracle.
required_inputs: Platform specification showing Strata CPU/OS ownership and the CPU-to-SMM RTC transport, connector and endpoint
Exact OS RTC device/driver plus any controller/bus/address/register mapping and read-only command allowlist
RTC time encoding, latch/rollover behavior, valid/oscillator/battery status interpretation, reference clock and tolerance
Physical inspection procedure, prohibited operations, bus/clock error limits, aborts and recovery
safety_requirements: Use only read-only commands on the verified CPU/OS RTC interface and correlate it to the SMM endpoint
Do not accept a BMC bus scan as proof of CPU/OS RTC access unless the approved architecture explicitly establishes that proxy relationship
Do not set system or RTC time, write RTC/EEPROM/control registers, clear logs, reset the bus/device or probe unknown addresses
Account for RTC latch, BCD encoding and second-boundary rollover when comparing samples
Stop on wrong-device mapping, oscillator-stop/invalid status, backward or implausible time, bus errors or management instability; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate the CPU/OS-to-SMM RTC architecture, physical population, device/driver mapping, safe read commands and time oracle
After operator confirmation, capture OS RTC inventory, binding/status and multiple timestamped read-only samples
Compare progression and reference tolerance while preserving kernel/RTC/I2C/management errors
Do not substitute BMC reachability, infer an address, set a clock, write a register, reset a controller or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve CPU/OS versus BMC ownership/proxy and the exact SMM RTC physical/logical path
Approve the RTC device/register/status semantics, read-only commands, trusted reference, tolerance and photo evidence
Review path-bound time/electrical evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A BMC `i2cdetect`/`i2cget` check may establish a separate management-side endpoint but does not prove the stated CPU/OS RTC read path. A host-side read such as an approved `/sys/class/rtc`/driver status query and `hwclock --show` is applicable only after exact device mapping.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the owner-approved read-only CPU/OS RTC device query on the mapped SMM endpoint, capture driver/status plus repeated time samples against the trusted reference, and pair it with operator physical evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Strata CPU-to-RTC-on-SMM scope and 10/10-minute allocation remain; interface, device, register and tolerance are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.status: MEDIUM CPU/OS-OWNERSHIP-BOUND SMM RTC PHYSICAL AND TIME-READ CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: First prove the physical/logical CPU-to-SMM RTC path, then collect device-bound read-only driver/status evidence and multiple time samples that advance coherently within the approved tolerance.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds ownership disambiguation, RTC device/driver identity, status/encoding semantics, rollover-aware sampling, reference tolerance and safe recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: BMC-side address visibility can pass while the host RTC driver is absent, bound to a different RTC or unable to read valid time; one unqualified timestamp also misses stopped or invalid RTC behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: RTC chips may expose clear-on-read or writable control/time registers, and naïve sampling across a second rollover can create false mismatches.

project_override_considerations: The source explicitly says CPU/OS, so default BMC/platform-management ownership cannot replace host-path evidence. A BMC proxy is acceptable only if the approved architecture proves it represents the same CPU/OS-to-SMM RTC path and the CPU/OS read is still demonstrated.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, authorization and approved CPU/OS-to-SMM RTC architecture
Operator photos identifying the CPU/SMM/RTC connection and populated endpoint
RTC device/driver and any controller/bus/address/register map with exact approved read-only commands
Complete RTC inventory/status plus multiple timestamped samples showing valid progression and reference-clock tolerance
Pre/post kernel/RTC/I2C/BMC error evidence and stable system/management state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require a CPU/OS-to-RTC-on-SMM connection and time read. The BMC-only method appears in the reference review, not in the authoritative source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The CPU/OS RTC communication objective is clear. Architecture, identity, time semantics, physical evidence and tolerance are supplyable prerequisites.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2163 Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00050-V002: approve the Strata CPU/OS versus BMC ownership/proxy and exact CPU-to-SMM RTC physical/logical interface; RTC device/driver and any controller/bus/address/register identity; read-only command and time encoding/latch/rollover/status semantics; trusted reference/tolerance, physical photo procedure, prohibited operations, aborts, and recovery.

review_improvement: Prevents a management-side RTC address from falsely satisfying the required CPU/OS time-read path and adds device-bound, rollover-aware, read-only time validity evidence plus physical proof.
independent_technical_reasoning: The acceptance subject is the CPU/OS, not an arbitrary platform-management master. RTC reachability must therefore be demonstrated at the OS-visible RTC device and correlated to the SMM endpoint. A single scan or timestamp cannot establish driver binding, clock progression, validity bits or accuracy. Repeated read-only samples with known encoding and rollover treatment are necessary, while writes and clock setting would alter the condition under test and create service-wide time risk.
